messages:
alex (support): heads up — customer acme-inc is seeing intermittent 502/401s after they moved traffic to our PrivateLink endpoint in us-east-1. first noticed ~08:12. details below, reproduction attached.

kevin (oncall): ok — which account/endpoint? any recent route-table changes?

alex (support): account acme-inc, vpce-0abc12345, endpoint in subnet-03a5, region us-east-1. They report DNS sometimes resolving to vpce IP 10.10.4.5, sometimes to public 54.23.12.7. curl returns 502 body: "upstream response timed out" then 401 from same client later.

tess (support): do we have client ip logs and tls handshake errors? ask for dig + curl output and traceroute

alex (support): pasted client repro (from customer's dev box):
```
# dig +short api.acme.example.internal
10.10.4.5
# dig +short api.acme.example.internal @169.254.169.254
54.23.12.7
# curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://api.acme.example.internal/v1/health --silent --show-error --max-time 5
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
{"error":"upstream timeout"}
# same command 30s later
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid token"}
```

sophie (eng-infra): that dig to 169.254.169.254 is weird — looks like their DHCP option sets a different resolver or they run local resolver that sometimes forwards to IGW. Need their /etc/resolv.conf and VPC DHCP options. Also check VPCE private-dns association.

kevin (oncall): can we reproduce from our test account with same rtbs and policy?

sophie (eng-infra): yes I'll spin up an instance in same AZ/subnet and attach the endpoint's route table. Also check SG, NACL, and endpoint policy. Quick checklist: 
- VPCE private DNS enabled? 
- Hostnames resolving to vpce ipv4? 
- Route table has prefix-list or is pointing to local? 
- Security group allows 443 ingress from client subnet? 
- Outbound to redwood backend allowed (NAT or IGW?)

alex (support): customer confirms PrivateDNS was NOT enabled when they created the endpoint — they manually added a CNAME in route53 that points to api.example.com. They also have a NAT gateway in same subnet for egress.

tess (support): that can cause split-horizon. If sometimes querying resolver that doesn't have private zone, they'll hit public record -> public ip -> requests go over internet to hosted api which expects a different client auth header or IP allowlist -> 401 or 502 depending on path.

alex (support): customer attached traceroute:
```
traceroute to api.acme.example.internal (54.23.12.7), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.4.10  0.6 ms  0.7 ms  0.6 ms
 2  52.95.1.1  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.0 ms
 ...
```

sophie (eng-infra): repro plan: step 1 enable Private DNS on VPCE OR create proper route53 private hosted zone for acme.example.internal and associate with VPCs. Step 2: remove public CNAME / ensure internal resolvers prefer VPC resolver (AmazonProvidedDNS at .2). Step 3: ensure SG on VPCE allows port 443 from client subnets and egress rules allow connections to backend subnets (or NAT config). Also confirm endpoint policy doesn't deny some calls.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: test-vpce-repro-env -> starting instance in us-east-1a (i-0fabc123)

kevin (oncall): while we wait, ask customer to run `dig +trace api.acme.example.internal` and `cat /etc/resolv.conf` and paste. Also ask for a tcpdump showing TLS handshake if possible.

alex (support): sent instructions. customer replied with /etc/resolv.conf showing custom 10.8.0.2 (their internal resolver) and dig +trace shows recursion via their onprem forwarder to public records. They said they put a conditional forwarder in the resolver for .example.internal to corporate onprem and forgot to add VPC private zone.

sophie (eng-infra): ok root cause = split-horizon DNS because private DNS not configured + conditional forwarder to onprem. That explains alternating 10.10.4.5 vs 54.23.12.7. 401s occur when traffic hits hosted public api which validates IPs/token audience differently; 502s when backend route from public hits our infra with mismatched host header -> timeout.

tess (support): mitigation: ask customer to enable Private DNS for the VPCE AND remove the public CNAME / remove conditional forwarder for that zone; or create private hosted zone in Route53 and associate with VPC. Also temporary workaround: set client /etc/hosts mapping api.acme.example.internal -> 10.10.4.5 on app nodes.

alex (support): customer applied private hosted zone and changed DNS; after TTL they report 0 errors for 45 minutes.

kevin (oncall): mark resolved, recommend we add a KB article about PrivateLink + conditional forwarder pitfalls and a checklist for onboarding with VPCE private DNS. I'll draft.

sophie (eng-infra): also add an alert to backend to log requests coming from public IPs to flag misrouted traffic.

tess (support): closing thread when KB created. :white_check_mark:
